seo.shareDescription: How the sensor works, what it measures, and how the data flows.

hero.title: Common
hero.body: Clear answers about the sensor, the measurements, data transfer, and current availability.

questions.question: How does Vēna measure blood pressure continuously?
questions.answer: A soft sensor is worn over an arterial site, such as the wrist or foot. The sensor detects pulse-related pressure changes and converts them into systolic, diastolic, and mean arterial pressure trends.

questions.question: Is it accurate compared to invasive monitoring?
questions.answer: In validation studies, Vēna has shown mean error under 3 mmHg compared with radial arterial line measurements. Full study data are available on request.

questions.question: Where is the sensor worn?
questions.answer: Either the inner wrist (over the radial artery) or the top of the foot. Both sites yield a clean beat-to-beat waveform; clinicians choose based on patient and workflow.

questions.question: How does the data reach the chart?
questions.answer: The sensor sends data over Bluetooth to the bedside iPad. From there, readings can be forwarded to a monitor, dashboard, health record workflow, or research database.

questions.question: What is the regulatory status?
questions.answer: Vēna is an investigational device. Performance claims reference internal validation and ongoing studies. Commercial availability is subject to regulatory clearance in each geography.

questions.question: Can patients wear it at home?
questions.answer: Yes. Vēna is designed for hospital, ambulatory, and home use, including post-procedure follow-up, medication titration, and decentralized clinical trials.
